handback.t:
W7 verdict: the quantum-inspired solvers (SA, parallel tempering, QAOA-style) are REJECTED. They win in only one independent world generator, and in that world exact and greedy search on the same learned model do as well or better. Part B (feature->agent) has no win. Everything is classical, with no quantum claims, no new crates, no edits to src/*.rs and no commits.

**What I built**
- Everything is in `src/bin/g7_qinspired.rs` and `src/bin/g7_common/{mod,world,solve,pols}.rs`. There are 6 unit tests, all pass.
- Part A (team assignment) learns a QUBO-style cost model online from team reward, then solves it with SA/PT/QAOA-style at 300 move-evaluations per decision. Ablations use the same model with exact search, greedy search, and an additive-only model.
- Part B (feature->agent) learns a binary assignment matrix Z (one agent per feature) with a load-penalty term, re-solved every 20 observations.
- Worlds are fixed in the `world.rs` header:
  - Part A has six worlds: separable control `A-sep`; coverage worlds `A-cover` and `A-cover-L`; planted-synergy worlds `A-syn`, `A-syn-drift` and `A-syn-L` (N=30, K=6).
  - Part B has three worlds: separable control `B-sep`, congested `B-cong`, and `B-cong-drift`.
- Baselines are keyword, eps-greedy, pooled-thompson, hebbian-robust, warm(hebr) and guarded-safe, each tuned per world on seeds 1-8. For teams I added two variants: K sequential selects with every member credited the team reward, and the real NeuralMesh with team_size=K.
- Protocol: held 31-60 and fresh 61-90 with frozen configs, paired 95% t-CI against the best fair baseline per world, Holm over 49 cells. The optimizer config is one pooled config across worlds (conservative); `--tune perworld` tunes it per world, as generously as the baselines.
- Compute is reported as evals/decision and ns/decision for every arm, plus an SA iteration sweep in the logs.

**Results (held | confirm)**
- Planted synergy (`A-syn`, `A-syn-drift`, `A-syn-L`): all Holm WINs, one generator.
  - `A-syn`: SA +0.165 | +0.159, PT +0.162 | +0.166, QAOA +0.163 | +0.162 over mesh(guarded-safe) at about 0.67.
  - `A-syn-L`: SA +0.106 | +0.110, PT +0.044 | +0.052, QAOA +0.032 | +0.039 (QAOA not significant on held).
- Coverage (`A-cover`, `A-cover-L`), a second generator: SA/PT/QAOA gains are at most +0.015. Only `A-cover-L` SA is a Holm WIN on confirm (+0.011); on held every annealing arm is not significant.
- Separable control `A-sep` is not harmless: SA -0.026 | -0.028, PT -0.038 | -0.023, exact -0.035 | -0.018, with a -0.07..-0.08 loss in the last quarter.
- The solver is not the source. On the same learned model, exact and greedy match or beat annealing at lower cost: `A-syn` exact +0.177 | +0.166 and greedy +0.174 | +0.167 versus SA +0.165 | +0.159. At 300 evals on N=30, greedy (+0.148 | +0.165, 5.5 us/decision) beats SA (+0.106 | +0.110, 19.6 us), and PT/QAOA are worse. SA only passes greedy at about 3000 evals (+0.013, 25x the compute).
- Cost per decision (single thread): mesh about 3-6 us, annealers 15-24 us, greedy 1-5.5 us, exact 3-9 us.
- Part B (feature->agent): no Holm WIN in any world on either set.
  - Drift world: SA -0.022 | -0.027 and QAOA -0.031 | -0.029 (QAOA a Holm LOSS on both sets; SA a LOSS on confirm only).
  - Decoupled argmax and greedy-polish are about as good as the annealers, so the load coupling does not help.
  - A cheating static-balanced-assignment ceiling that knows the hidden table gets 0.77 versus about 0.66 for the best fair baseline. That headroom is real, but no learner here reaches it.
- Per-world tuning of the optimizer does not change these verdicts.
- By-product, not quantum-inspired: the learned team model with greedy search beats the repo's mesh and sequential routers.
  - `q-greedy` is +0.13..+0.17 in the synergy worlds and +0.016 in `A-cover-L` (Holm WIN on both sets).
  - The additive-only variant `qadd-greedy` is +0.027 in `A-cover-L` (WIN both sets), and +0.09..+0.14 in the synergy worlds.
  - It costs about 1-3 points on the separable control, and the synergy worlds match its model class by construction.
  - I recommend it only as a separate follow-up, not for defaults.

**Process caveats (also in the board entry)**
- I looked at held 31-60 numbers before making four changes:
  - widened the Part B `lam` grid (the tuner hit its edge);
  - added the optimism knob `pm_other`;
  - added `--tune perworld`;
  - added `A-cover-L`, included regardless of outcome.
- Later development checks used a separate `--set dev` (seeds 101-130). Confirm 61-90 was run only on the final binary, and verdicts agree on both sets.
- Timings are wall-clock on a shared box, so use evals/decision for exact comparisons.

**Rerun (director)**
Set the PATH line from the brief, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r5` and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=3`, then from `C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh`, each run about 2-3 min and deterministic:
- `cargo test --release --offline --bin g7_qinspired`
- `cargo run --release --offline --bin g7_qinspired -- --set held --out results/g7_qinspired.json`
- same with `--set confirm --out results/g7_qinspired_confirm61-90.json`
- add `--tune perworld` for the generous variants.
